domain: Ambient environment sensing on iOS 26 / iOS 27 beta (July 2026) — SensorKit, SoundAnalysis, audio/light/pressure/magnetic proxies, and weather enrichment — scoped to a personally sideloaded quantified-self app where the owner is the subject. iOS 27 is at developer beta 4 (July 20, 2026), public beta since July 13; GA expected ~Sept 14, 2026. iOS 26 is the shipping release. All API facts below were verified against the live DocC JSON backing developer.apple.com, which currently serves the iOS 27 beta SDK.

capabilities.stream: Ambient light: illuminance in lux + CIE chromaticity (x,y) + sensor placement (front/back)
capabilities.permission: NSSensorKitUsageDescription + NSSensorKitPrivacyPolicyURL + NSSensorKitUsageDetail[SRSensorUsageAmbientLightSensor]. Consent is a system 'Research Sensor & Usage Data Request' sheet, per-sensor, revocable in Settings > Privacy > Research Sensor & Usage Data — NOT a standard alert.
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.sensorkit.reader.allow (ARRAY of per-sensor strings; this one is 'ambient-light-sensor')
capabilities.resolution: Event-driven on ALS change; historical fetch only
capabilities.backfill: None at install. After startRecording(), a rolling 7 days of prior recorded data — but the most recent 24h is withheld (see blockers/nonObvious)
capabilities.notes: THE definitive ambient-light stream on iOS — the only public API exposing true lux. Unobtainable without the gated entitlement; see blockers.

capabilities.stream: Ambient barometric pressure + device temperature (SensorKit stream)
capabilities.notes: Gated. The FREE substitute (CMAltimeter) gives the same physical quantity with only NSMotionUsageDescription — see that row.

capabilities.stream: Raw 3-axis acceleration, continuously recorded
capabilities.notes: Gated. Free-ish analogue = CMSensorRecorder (contested availability) or a foreground CMMotionManager.

capabilities.stream: Raw 3-axis rotation rate (gyroscope), continuously recorded
capabilities.notes: Gated. Shares the SRSensorUsageMotion plist key with accelerometer.

capabilities.stream: Frequently-visited places: coordinate, arrival/departure timestamps, distance from home/work, location category
capabilities.notes: Gated. FREE substitute = CoreLocation CLVisit, which is nearly as good and background-relaunches your app. Use that.

capabilities.stream: Step count, distance, floors, pace, cadence (recorded stream)
capabilities.notes: Gated — and pointless to chase, since CMPedometer.queryPedometerData gives the identical type free with 7-day backfill.

capabilities.stream: Device usage: screen wake/unlock counts, app usage by category, notification counts, web-domain usage
capabilities.resolution: Aggregated reports over a fetch interval
capabilities.notes: Gated. No free equivalent — Screen Time (DeviceActivity/FamilyControls) is a separate, also-gated framework.

capabilities.stream: Messages app usage: counts of sent/received messages (no content)
capabilities.notes: Gated. No message content is ever exposed — counts only.

capabilities.stream: Phone call usage: total time on calls, incoming/outgoing/missed counts (no numbers or audio)
capabilities.notes: Gated.

capabilities.stream: Keyboard metrics: typing speed, key/word/sentence counts, typo & autocorrect rates, path-typing, emoji counts, per-key touch-down/up distances
capabilities.notes: Gated. This is the richest cognitive/motor-tremor proxy Apple exposes anywhere — heavily used in Parkinson's and depression research. No free substitute exists.

capabilities.stream: Watch on-wrist state (on/off wrist, crown orientation, wrist side, band-fit)
capabilities.notes: Gated. Fetched from the paired Watch via SRFetchRequest.device.

capabilities.stream: Media interaction events in messaging apps (images/videos viewed, sent, saved)
capabilities.notes: Gated.

capabilities.stream: Voice metrics from Siri interactions: pitch, tenor, cadence, words-per-minute, inter-word pauses, plus SRSpeechExpression affect features
capabilities.notes: Gated. Apple explicitly strips raw audio AND transcript strings — metrics only. Shares the SRSensorUsageSpeechMetrics key with telephonySpeechMetrics.

capabilities.stream: Voice metrics during phone calls: pitch, tenor, cadence, timing
capabilities.notes: Gated. No raw audio. This is the single most privacy-sensitive SensorKit stream and a likely reason the whole framework is IRB-gated.

capabilities.stream: Face metrics: ARKit blendshape/expression coefficients describing the user's face during device use
capabilities.api: SRSensor.faceMetrics → SRFaceMetrics (uses ARKit; guarded by SR_ARKIT_SUPPORTED)
capabilities.notes: Gated. Requires TrueDepth hardware.

capabilities.stream: High-frequency heart rate from Apple Watch (beat-level, not the 5-min HealthKit summary)
capabilities.notes: Gated. HealthKit heartRate is the free fallback but at much lower temporal resolution.

capabilities.stream: Odometer: travel speed and terrain slope
capabilities.notes: Gated. Slope is an environment signal (hills, stairs, terrain) not otherwise exposed.

capabilities.stream: Wrist skin temperature during sleep (session + per-sample series)
capabilities.notes: Gated. Free fallback = HealthKit appleSleepingWristTemperature (nightly deviation, coarser). Series 8+/Ultra required.

capabilities.stream: Raw photoplethysmogram (PPG) waveform — the optical signal underlying heart rate
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.sensorkit.reader.allow — REQUIRES the explicit 'ppg' string in the entitlement array
capabilities.notes: Gated, and doubly so — 'ppg' is called out as a separate entitlement string in Apple's own docs, implying independent approval. Nothing else on iOS exposes raw PPG.

capabilities.stream: Raw electrocardiogram (ECG) waveform samples
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.sensorkit.reader.allow — REQUIRES the explicit 'ecg' string in the entitlement array
capabilities.notes: Gated. HealthKit HKElectrocardiogram is the free fallback and DOES give voltage measurements for user-initiated ECG readings — a genuinely viable substitute.

capabilities.stream: Acoustic settings (audio routing/volume/output configuration state)
capabilities.notes: NEW IN iOS 26. Documentation is still a raw header-comment stub ('This stream stores samples of the Acoustic Settings sensor') — no abstract, no plist key published yet.

capabilities.stream: Sleep sessions (session boundaries and structure, SensorKit-side)
capabilities.notes: NEW IN iOS 26. Doc stub contains Apple's own typo ('Sesnor stream for sleep sessions collection'). HealthKit HKCategoryValueSleepAnalysis is the free substitute and is quite good.

capabilities.stream: AirPods head motion: acceleration, rotation rate, and altitude, continuously recorded
capabilities.notes: NEW IN iOS 27 BETA, flagged beta:true in DocC. Notably includes ALTITUDE from AirPods. Free substitute = CMHeadphoneMotionManager (foreground/live only, no recording).

capabilities.stream: AirPods settings state (ANC/transparency mode, volume, fit)
capabilities.notes: NEW IN iOS 27 BETA. Pairs with HealthKit environmentalSoundReduction, which gives the acoustic effect of ANC for free.

capabilities.stream: Ambient sound classification — 303 labels incl. speech, snoring, typing, traffic_noise, rain, thunderstorm, dog_bark, vacuum_cleaner, microwave_oven, toilet_flush, water_tap_faucet, air_conditioner, mechanical_fan, siren, silence, and 288 more
capabilities.permission: NSMicrophoneUsageDescription (runtime mic prompt). Background needs UIBackgroundModes = 'audio' and, per developer reports, ALSO 'processing'.
capabilities.resolution: Default windowDuration ~0.975s; configurable via windowDurationConstraint; overlapFactor default 0.5
capabilities.notes: 100% on-device, no network, no entitlement — the single best FREE ambient-environment sensor on iOS. VERIFIED: .version1 is still the ONLY SNClassifierIdentifier case in the iOS 27 beta docs. CAVEAT: the 303-label list is a community dump taken at iOS 15.0; a stable identifier does not prove the model behind it never changed, and I could not run knownClassifications on-device to confirm. Treat 303 as 'the published list, unverified against iOS 26'. Battery: continuous mic + CoreML inference is heavy — expect meaningful drain; duty-cycle it (e.g. 10s every 5min) rather than running continuously.

capabilities.stream: Instantaneous ambient sound level (relative), for continuous dB logging
capabilities.api: AVAudioRecorder.isMeteringEnabled = true; .updateMeters(); .averagePower(forChannel:) / .peakPower(forChannel:). Set AVAudioSession.Mode.measurement on .record or .playAndRecord.
capabilities.resolution: As fast as you call updateMeters() — practically 10–60 Hz
capabilities.notes: CRITICAL DISTINCTION: this returns dBFS (decibels full-scale), range −160 to 0, UNCALIBRATED and relative to the ADC's full scale. It is NOT sound pressure level. HealthKit environmentalAudioExposure by contrast is absolute, A-weighted dBASPL calibrated by Apple. To approximate SPL you must add an empirically-determined offset per device model — there is no API for it. Always set Mode.measurement or automatic gain control silently compresses your readings and destroys comparability.

capabilities.stream: Absolute ambient sound pressure level, A-weighted, calibrated
capabilities.entitlement: none (HealthKit capability is available on a free personal team)
capabilities.resolution: Apple Watch samples roughly continuously in ~1-min equivalent-continuous windows; iPhone contributes less often
capabilities.backfill: FULL — every sample ever written to the HealthKit store is queryable on first launch
capabilities.notes: This is the answer to the calibration problem: Apple already runs a calibrated dBASPL pipeline on the Watch and stores it in HealthKit. No mic permission, no battery cost, and years of retroactive history. For ambient-dB quantified self, this beats rolling your own AVAudioSession meter.

capabilities.stream: Environmental sound reduction achieved by ANC headphones (dBASPL delta)
capabilities.resolution: Discrete equivalent-continuous samples while wearing supported headphones
capabilities.notes: Auto-collected by AirPods Pro/Max. Free proxy for 'am I in noise-cancelling mode', i.e. an acoustic-environment context signal.

capabilities.stream: Headphone audio exposure (dBASPL) — what you are dosing yourself with
capabilities.notes: Auto-detected by iPhone OR Watch. Pairs with environmentalAudioExposure to separate self-inflicted from ambient noise dose.

capabilities.stream: Time spent in daylight (minutes/day) — a bright-light exposure proxy
capabilities.resolution: Cumulative daily totals, built from Watch ambient-light sampling
capabilities.notes: THE most important free finding for ambient light. Apple derives this from the Watch's ambient light sensor (threshold ~1000 lux) — it is a lux-derived signal you can get with zero entitlement, zero approval, and full retroactive history. It is the practical stand-in for SensorKit ambientLightSensor for circadian work. Requires Apple Watch Series 6+ / SE 2.

capabilities.stream: UV index exposure
capabilities.api: HKQuantityTypeIdentifier.uvExposure (count units, discrete; value = UV index during sample duration)
capabilities.notes: No Apple hardware writes this automatically — it is a write-target for third-party UV sensors or your own app. You can populate it yourself from WeatherKit/Open-Meteo UV index + location, turning HealthKit into your enrichment store.

capabilities.stream: Water temperature (°C) of the surrounding water
capabilities.resolution: Discrete samples during dive/swim workouts; may be condensed/coalesced
capabilities.notes: Apple Watch Ultra only. This is the ONLY ambient (non-body) temperature Apple exposes anywhere on iOS — the iPhone's internal thermistors are not accessible.

capabilities.stream: Underwater depth (m) — ambient hydrostatic pressure derived
capabilities.notes: Apple Watch Ultra depth gauge.

capabilities.stream: Raw barometric pressure (kPa) + relative altitude change — the FREE barometer
capabilities.permission: NSMotionUsageDescription (app CRASHES if the key is absent)
capabilities.resolution: ~1 Hz, regardless of whether the value changed
capabilities.notes: This is the free equivalent of SensorKit ambientPressure and gives the same physical quantity. Excellent for weather-front detection, indoor/outdoor transitions, floor changes, and HVAC/door-opening pressure transients. Very low battery cost. Works in background with the location background mode or a background task.

capabilities.stream: Absolute altitude above sea level (m) with accuracy + precision
capabilities.notes: Apple states explicitly: iPhone 12 and later, and Apple Watch Series 6 / SE and later ONLY. Fuses barometer with GPS/map data, so it is sea-level-referenced rather than relative.

capabilities.stream: Ambient pressure + temperature pair (submersion-capable devices)
capabilities.minIOS: 10.0 (type); water submersion APIs are Watch Ultra / watchOS 9+
capabilities.notes: The .temperature here is the closest thing to a free ambient-temperature reading, but it is only populated on Apple Watch Ultra during water submersion.

capabilities.stream: Magnetic field vector (µT, 3-axis) — EMF / indoor-structure / appliance-proximity signal
capabilities.api: CMMotionManager.startMagnetometerUpdates(to:withHandler:) → CMMagnetometerData.magneticField (CMMagneticField x/y/z, raw incl. device bias); or CMDeviceMotion.magneticField for a calibrated CMCalibratedMagneticField with .accuracy
capabilities.permission: none for raw magnetometer (no usage-description key required); NSMotionUsageDescription needed if combined with pedometer/activity APIs
capabilities.notes: A genuinely underused ambient sensor. Indoor steel structure, elevators, motors, transformers, laptops and induction cooktops all produce distinctive magnetic signatures — useful as an indoor/outdoor and room-identity classifier. Background operation requires an active background mode (audio/location) to keep the app running; CoreMotion itself will not wake you.

capabilities.stream: Compass heading + magnetic/true north deviation
capabilities.notes: headingAccuracy degrading sharply is itself an environment signal — it indicates local magnetic interference (indoors, vehicles, near electronics).

capabilities.stream: Arrival/departure at meaningful places (the free 'visits' sensor)
capabilities.resolution: Per-visit arrival/departure events; very low power (uses the same infrastructure as significant-location-change)
capabilities.backfill: none — events begin at monitoring start
capabilities.notes: BEST FREE SUBSTITUTE for SensorKit .visits. Apple explicitly documents that if the app is terminated while active, the SYSTEM RELAUNCHES IT to deliver visit events — true unattended background collection with no background mode declared. Works without precise-location authorization (falls back to reduced accuracy). No-op in visionOS.

capabilities.stream: Historical step count / distance / floors ascended+descended / pace / cadence
capabilities.resolution: Query any window; live updates roughly per-second
capabilities.backfill: ~7 DAYS of system-cached history available on first launch
capabilities.notes: floorsAscended/floorsDescended are barometer-derived and act as an indoor-vertical-movement signal. The 7-day backfill means a fresh install immediately has a week of data — one of the few APIs where that's true.

capabilities.stream: Motion context: stationary / walking / running / automotive / cycling, with confidence
capabilities.resolution: Event on activity change; Apple warns of 'a delay of up to several minutes' in reported activities
capabilities.backfill: ~7 DAYS — 'The system stores only the last seven days worth of activity data at most'
capabilities.notes: Free indoor/outdoor and transport-mode classifier. Flags are NOT mutually exclusive (stopped at a red light = automotive AND stationary both true), and all can be false. Empty ranges return CMErrorUnknown rather than an empty array — handle that.

capabilities.stream: Background-recorded raw accelerometer (the free CMSensorRecorder path)
capabilities.api: CMSensorRecorder.recordAccelerometer(forDuration:) then accelerometerData(from:to:) → CMSensorDataList; gate on isAccelerometerRecordingAvailable() and isAuthorizedForRecording()
capabilities.resolution: 50 Hz fixed; records up to 12h per call
capabilities.backfill: Up to ~3 days of previously recorded data retrievable
capabilities.notes: CONTESTED. (a) One widely-cited claim is that 'Apple removed all documentation' for this API — I REFUTE that directly: I fetched the live DocC JSON from the iOS 27 beta doc set and the page is present and current. (b) The real dispute is RUNTIME availability: developers report isAccelerometerRecordingAvailable() returning false on many iPhones, with one source attributing it to an A10-or-newer hardware threshold (true on iPhone XR, false on SE/6s Plus) and another attributing it to Motion & Fitness authorization state rather than hardware. Apple has never documented the hardware requirement. Verdict: implement it, but treat availability as a runtime probe, not a guarantee. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/15470 · https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/113845

capabilities.stream: AirPods head orientation, acceleration, rotation rate, gravity (live)
capabilities.api: CMHeadphoneMotionManager.startDeviceMotionUpdates(to:withHandler:) → CMDeviceMotion; also startConnectionStatusUpdates() for wear/connection state
capabilities.permission: NSMotionUsageDescription (app crashes if absent when starting device-motion updates)
capabilities.notes: Requires motion-capable AirPods (Pro, Max, 3rd gen+). Head pose is a posture/attention signal; connection-status updates tell you when AirPods are worn. Free counterpart to the iOS 27 beta SensorKit headphoneMotion sensor, but without recording/backfill.

capabilities.stream: Scene light level (lumens proxy) + color temperature (Kelvin) from the camera
capabilities.api: ARSession with isLightEstimationEnabled = true → ARFrame.lightEstimate → ARLightEstimate.ambientIntensity (lumens, 1000 = neutral) and .ambientColorTemperature (Kelvin, 6500 = neutral)
capabilities.resolution: Per ARFrame — 60 Hz while the session runs
capabilities.notes: FOREGROUND AND CAMERA-SESSION ONLY. ARSession suspends when the app backgrounds, and the orange camera indicator is unavoidable — this is not a covert or ambient logger, it's a spot-measurement tool. ambientIntensity is a relative estimate, not calibrated lux; ambientColorTemperature is genuinely useful for circadian work (warm indoor vs daylight vs screen-lit). Practical pattern: sample it deliberately a few times a day rather than continuously.

capabilities.stream: Directional light environment: spherical harmonics (2nd order, RGB), primary light direction and intensity
capabilities.notes: Richer than plain ARLightEstimate — ARKit uses the detected face as a light probe. Gives you the DIRECTION light comes from, not just the amount. Requires TrueDepth hardware. Same foreground-only limitation.

capabilities.stream: Camera exposure parameters as a light proxy: ISO, exposure duration, aperture, exposure target offset
capabilities.api: AVCaptureDevice.iso, .exposureDuration (CMTime), .lensAperture, .exposureTargetOffset — all key-value observable; format bounds via activeFormat.minISO/maxISO/minExposureDuration/maxExposureDuration
capabilities.resolution: KVO — updates as fast as the exposure algorithm converges
capabilities.notes: Lighter-weight alternative to spinning up ARKit for a light reading. Because EV ≈ log2(aperture² / exposureDuration) − log2(ISO/100), you can derive a repeatable relative-luminance figure from a locked-format capture session — more stable across sessions than ARKit's ambientIntensity. Still foreground-only with a visible camera indicator.

capabilities.stream: Screen brightness as a zero-permission ambient-light proxy
capabilities.permission: none — no usage description, no prompt, nothing
capabilities.resolution: Poll at any rate; KVO-able on UIScreen
capabilities.notes: Cheapest ambient-light signal on the platform. When auto-brightness is enabled in Settings, this value is driven by the ambient light sensor — so it is an indirect ALS readout requiring NO permission at all. Confounded by manual adjustment and by Low Power Mode. Note Apple's caveat: if you SET it, the change persists until device lock. Read-only use is safe.

capabilities.stream: Local weather enrichment: current conditions, minute precipitation, hourly/daily forecast, severe alerts, UV index, pressure + pressure trend, wind, cloud cover, sun/moon events, historical comparisons
capabilities.api: WeatherService.shared.weather(for:) → Weather (CurrentWeather, MinuteWeather, HourWeather, DayWeather, WeatherAlert, SunEvents, MoonEvents, UVIndex, PressureTrend, CloudCoverByAltitude, HistoricalComparisons, DailyWeatherStatistics)
capabilities.permission: NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription (to get coordinates); WeatherKit itself prompts nothing
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.weatherkit (Boolean) — enable the WeatherKit capability in Xcode; REQUIRES a paid Apple Developer Program membership
capabilities.resolution: Minute-level precipitation for ~1h; hourly to 10 days; daily to 10 days
capabilities.backfill: Limited — HistoricalComparisons / DailyWeatherStatistics give climatological baselines, not arbitrary historical observations
capabilities.notes: 500,000 API calls/month included with ADP membership ($99/yr). NOT usable on a free Apple ID — the capability must be registered against an App ID on the developer portal, which a personal team cannot do. Attribution (logo + link) is legally required. Given Pillar 3 (prefer the free path), Open-Meteo is the better default.

capabilities.stream: Local weather enrichment, keyless: temperature, apparent temperature, humidity, dewpoint, surface + sea-level pressure, cloud cover (low/mid/high), visibility, wind at 10/80/120/180 m, gusts, precipitation/rain/showers/snowfall, weather code, UV index, sunshine + daylight duration, shortwave/direct/diffuse radiation, CAPE, vapour-pressure deficit, evapotranspiration, soil temperature and moisture at multiple depths
capabilities.api: GET https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=..&longitude=..&current=..&hourly=..&daily=.. ; history via https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive (1940→present) and https://air-quality-api.open-meteo.com/v1/air-quality (PM2.5, PM10, ozone, NO2, SO2, CO, aerosol optical depth, dust, European + US AQI, birch/grass/ragweed pollen)
capabilities.permission: NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription (for coordinates only). No app-transport exception needed — HTTPS.
capabilities.entitlement: none — NO API KEY, NO ACCOUNT for non-commercial use
capabilities.resolution: Hourly and 15-minutely forecast; hourly historical archive back to 1940
capabilities.backfill: FULL — the archive endpoint serves hourly reanalysis data from 1940 to present for any coordinate, free
capabilities.notes: THE free-path winner, and strictly more capable than WeatherKit for quantified self. Documented free limits: 600 calls/min, 5,000/hour, 10,000/day, 300,000/month — far above WeatherKit's 500k/month and with no $99 gate. Non-commercial use is CC BY 4.0 (attribution required). The 1940-to-present archive means you can retroactively enrich your ENTIRE existing HealthKit history with weather, which WeatherKit cannot do. Air-quality endpoint adds pollen and PM2.5, which Apple exposes nowhere. Self-hostable (Docker) for total ownership.

capabilities.stream: Network context as an indoor/outdoor and location-identity signal
capabilities.notes: Zero permission, zero battery. Wi-Fi vs cellular is a strong indoor/outdoor and home/work proxy. NOTE the contrast: reading the actual Wi-Fi SSID/BSSID via CNCopyCurrentNetworkInfo requires the com.apple.developer.networking.wifi-info entitlement — that one is a paid-ADP capability you can self-enable with NO approval step, which makes it a good example of the middle tier between 'free' and 'Apple must approve you'.

capabilities.stream: Device thermal state as a coarse ambient-temperature / workload signal
capabilities.notes: Very coarse, heavily confounded by CPU load and charging. Only meaningful as an ambient-heat indicator when correlated with low device activity (e.g. phone idle in a hot car). Combine with UIDevice.batteryState — 'charging' is itself a strong home/car/desk context signal, also free via UIDevice.isBatteryMonitoringEnabled.

capabilities.stream: Proximity (near/far binary from the front IR sensor)
capabilities.notes: Binary only — no distance value. Signals 'phone against face/in pocket'. Blanks the screen while enabled, so it is intrusive for a always-on logger; use situationally.

capabilities.stream: Modern async SensorKit reader (Swift concurrency rewrite)
capabilities.api: SRReader<Sensor: SRDataSensor> — .samples(matching:), .deletionRecords(matching:), .startRecording(), .stopRecording(), .devices, .authorizationStatus; per-sensor generic types SRAmbientLightSensor, SRAmbientPressureSensor, SRAccelerometerSensor, SRAcousticSettingsSensor, SRDeviceUsageSensor, SRElectrocardiogramSensor, SRFaceMetricsSensor, SRHeadphoneMotionSensor, SRHeadphoneSettingsSensor, SRHeartRateSensor, SRKeyboardMetricsSensor, SRMediaEventsSensor, SRMessagesUsageSensor, SROdometerSensor, SROnWristStateSensor, SRPedometerDataSensor, SRPhoneUsageSensor, SRPhotoplethysmogramSensor, SRRotationRateSensor, SRSiriSpeechMetricsSensor, SRSleepSessionsSensor, SRTelephonySpeechMetricsSensor, SRVisitsSensor, SRWristTemperatureSensor
capabilities.notes: NEW IN iOS 27 BETA and previously undocumented anywhere. Replaces the delegate-based SRSensorReader with a type-safe generic + async/await design. Signals Apple is actively investing in SensorKit rather than deprecating it — but the entitlement gate is unchanged.

blockers: SENSORKIT IS UNOBTAINABLE FOR AN INDIVIDUAL — DEFINITIVE. Three independent gates each fatal on their own. (1) ACCOUNT TYPE: Apple's SensorKit request process requires 'Account type: Organization. Individual accounts are not accepted' — an Apple Developer Program ORGANIZATION account with a D-U-N-S number, with the Account Holder signing the SensorKit Addendum. A personal/individual ADP account is rejected before technical review. (2) STUDY APPROVAL: the entitlement doc states 'Apple only grants the entitlement for approved research studies.' Development entitlement needs a research proposal + signed SensorKit Addendum emailed to sensorkitrequest@apple.com; DISTRIBUTION additionally needs an IRB/Ethics Committee approval letter, an Informed Consent Form, signed Collaborator Agreements from every entity touching the data, and review by Apple's approval committee. Reported timeline: 5–7 days to first response, 8–14 weeks to grant. (3) CODE SIGNING: even with approval, Apple requires an EXPLICIT App ID with the sensor reader enabled under 'Additional Capabilities', a MANUAL provisioning profile, Code Signing Identity 'Apple Developer', and Code Signing Style 'Manual'. A free Apple ID (personal team) cannot register explicit App IDs with Additional Capabilities, cannot create manual provisioning profiles, and cannot sign restricted entitlements — amfid validates the entitlement against the certificate's allowed set at launch, and the system CLOSES the app if the signature lacks the entitlement. Re-signing via AltStore/Sideloadly does not help, because it re-signs with the same free-team identity. CONTESTED POINT, both sides given: researchandcare.org's page (Apple's own ResearchKit/CareKit site) says only that the app 'will need to be submitted and published under your developer account' and does NOT explicitly prohibit personal accounts; the Avicenna Research implementation guide states flatly that individual accounts are not accepted. I found NO first-hand report anywhere of an individual obtaining this entitlement for self-research. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/entitlements/com.apple.developer.sensorkit.reader.allow · https://developer.apple.com/documentation/sensorkit/configuring-your-project-for-sensor-reading · https://www.researchandcare.org/resources/accessing-sensorkit-data/ · https://forum.avicennaresearch.com/t/sensorkit-approval/1563

SENSORKIT 24-HOUR HOLDING PERIOD — and it fails SILENTLY. Apple, verbatim: 'SensorKit places a 24-hour holding period on newly recorded data before an app can access it. This gives the user an opportunity to delete any data they don't want to share with the app. A fetch request doesn't return any results if its time range overlaps this holding period.' Note the failure mode: not an error, not a partial result — ZERO results for the whole request if ANY part of the range touches the last 24h. Real-time SensorKit is therefore impossible by design, even with the entitlement. Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/sensorkit/srfetchrequest

SENSORKIT HAS NO RETROACTIVE BACKFILL. SRSensorReader.fetch() 'can retrieve only sensor data that the app records by first calling startRecording()'. You get a rolling 7-day window that starts accumulating only after your app calls startRecording() — there is no access to data the system collected before your app existed. Combined with the 24h hold, the usable window is roughly t−7d to t−24h. Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/sensorkit/srsensorreader

NO AMBIENT AIR TEMPERATURE ON iPHONE. The iPhone contains internal thermistors but exposes none of them publicly. The only ambient (non-body) temperature APIs are HealthKit waterTemperature and CMAmbientPressureData.temperature — BOTH Apple Watch Ultra, both only during water submersion. SensorKit ambientPressure also carries a .temperature field but it is device temperature, not room temperature, and is entitlement-gated regardless. For indoor air temperature you must use an external sensor or an Open-Meteo/WeatherKit outdoor reading as a proxy.

NO CALIBRATED LUX WITHOUT SENSORKIT. iOS exposes true lux in exactly one place: SRAmbientLightSample.lux, which is gated. Every free alternative is a proxy: ARKit ambientIntensity is an uncalibrated lumens ESTIMATE from the camera, AVCaptureDevice ISO/exposure is a derived relative EV, UIScreen.brightness is an indirect readout of auto-brightness, and HealthKit timeInDaylight is a thresholded binary aggregated to daily minutes. None is interchangeable with lux.

ARKIT LIGHT ESTIMATION CANNOT RUN IN BACKGROUND. ARSession suspends when the app is backgrounded, so ARFrame delivery stops and lightEstimate goes stale. The camera is required, and the orange camera-in-use indicator is unavoidable and cannot be suppressed. Same applies to AVCaptureDevice ISO/exposure. Any continuous ambient-light logging strategy built on the camera is not viable — treat these as manual spot readings.

AVAudioSession METERING IS NOT SOUND PRESSURE LEVEL. averagePower(forChannel:) returns dBFS in the range −160 to 0, referenced to the ADC's digital full scale, with no defined relationship to acoustic dB SPL. Converting to SPL requires a per-device-model offset that Apple does not publish and provides no API for. Do not report AVAudioSession numbers as decibels of ambient noise — use HealthKit environmentalAudioExposure, which IS A-weighted absolute dBASPL calibrated by Apple.

WEATHERKIT REQUIRES A PAID MEMBERSHIP. The com.apple.developer.weatherkit entitlement must be enabled as a capability against a registered App ID on the developer portal. A free Apple ID personal team cannot do this. The 500,000 free calls/month are 'included with an Apple Developer Program membership' ($99/yr), not with a free Apple ID. Open-Meteo is the free-path replacement and is strictly more capable for this use case.

WI-FI SSID/BSSID NEEDS AN ENTITLEMENT. CNCopyCurrentNetworkInfo requires com.apple.developer.networking.wifi-info. Unlike SensorKit this needs NO Apple approval — you self-enable it in the portal — but it still requires a PAID ADP account, so it is unavailable on a free Apple ID. NWPathMonitor's interface type (wifi vs cellular) is the free fallback and needs no permission at all.

FREE APPLE ID SIDELOADING CONSTRAINTS (apply to the whole app, not one API). A personal team's provisioning profiles expire after 7 days, requiring re-signing; you are limited to 3 sideloaded apps at a time and 10 App IDs per week; and restricted entitlements cannot be signed at all. Any design depending on uninterrupted multi-week background collection should account for the 7-day re-sign cycle — a re-signed app keeps its container, but the interruption is real.

SENSORKIT IGNORES MAC CATALYST AND visionOS. Apple states the framework 'ignores calls from Mac apps that you build with Mac Catalyst, and from compatible iPad and iPhone apps running in visionOS.' Separately, CLLocationManager.startMonitoringVisits() 'does nothing' when a compatible iPad/iPhone app runs in visionOS.

THE SOUNDANALYSIS 303-CLASS COUNT IS NOT VERIFIED FOR iOS 26. I confirmed SNClassifierIdentifier.version1 is still the only case in the iOS 27 beta documentation, but a stable identifier does not prove the underlying CoreML model's label set is unchanged. The 303-label roster above is a community dump captured at iOS 15.0. I could not run knownClassifications on-device (no Mac/Xcode/iOS device in this environment) and found no published re-dump for iOS 17/18/26. Treat the list as authoritative-as-published but re-run print(request.knownClassifications) on target hardware before relying on the exact count.
nonObvious: THE SENSORKIT ENTITLEMENT IS A PER-SENSOR STRING ARRAY, NOT A BOOLEAN. com.apple.developer.sensorkit.reader.allow takes an <array> of strings — 'on-wrist', 'ambient-light-sensor', 'motion-accelerometer', 'motion-rotation-rate', 'visits', 'pedometer', 'device-usage', 'messages-usage', 'phone-usage', 'keyboard-metrics', plus 'ecg' and 'ppg' which Apple calls out in separate code samples on their own sensor pages (implying they are approved independently and are harder to get). Approval is per-sensor, not for 'SensorKit'. The Avicenna guidance reinforces this: proposals must identify specific SensorKit data types, not request the framework generically.

THE 24-HOUR HOLD RETURNS AN EMPTY RESULT, NOT AN ERROR. If your fetch range overlaps the last 24 hours you get zero samples and a successful completion callback. A developer debugging 'why is my data empty' will look at authorization, recording state, and device selection long before suspecting a silent time-range rule. Always fetch t−7d to t−25h and never let the upper bound approach now().

startRecording() IS A HARD PREREQUISITE AND IT IS REFERENCE-COUNTED. fetch() returns nothing for any period before your app called startRecording(). Worse, the framework only starts the underlying sensor if it isn't already running for another app or system process, and calling stopRecording() 'relinquishes stakeholdership' — when no app or system process holds a stake, the sensor DEACTIVATES. So another app stopping its recording can change your data availability, and your own stopRecording() can silently end collection you assumed was continuous.

THE USER CAN RETROACTIVELY DELETE DATA OUT FROM UNDER YOUR DATASET — AND YOU CAN DETECT IT. SRDeletionRecord accounts for gaps in recorded data with a startTime, endTime and reason. Retrieving them uses a non-obvious trick: you construct a SECOND reader against a derived sensor name via an NSString extension — SRSensorReader(sensor: ambientLightSensor.rawValue.sr_sensorForDeletionRecordsFromSensor()). Nothing in the SRSensorReader API surface hints this exists. Without it, deleted spans are indistinguishable from sensor downtime, which silently corrupts any duty-cycle or adherence analysis.

SOUNDANALYSIS FAILED ON LOCKED DEVICES FOR TWO ENTIRE iOS RELEASES, WITH A GPU ERROR THAT NAMES THE REAL CAUSE. On iOS 18.0–18.1, background CoreML inference threw 'Insufficient Permission (to submit GPU work from background)' → 'Failed to evaluate model 0 in pipeline'. iOS restricts GPU work from background processes; SoundAnalysis's default CoreML compute units try the GPU. Two workarounds surfaced from developers: force CPU-only compute units, or additionally declare the 'processing' background mode alongside 'audio'. Reported fixed in iOS 18.2. This matters even on iOS 26/27: the underlying GPU-from-background restriction still exists, so if you ship a CUSTOM CoreML sound classifier, pin MLComputeUnits to .cpuOnly for background operation rather than assuming the platform handles it. Source: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/757715

AVAudioSession.Mode.measurement IS LOAD-BEARING FOR ANY dB LOGGING. Without it, iOS applies automatic gain control and dynamics processing to the input signal, so a quiet room and a loud room converge toward the same meter reading and your time series becomes meaningless. Setting .measurement 'disables some dynamics processing on input and output signals' and, on multi-mic devices, pins the session to the primary microphone — which also removes cross-device variance from beamforming. This single line is the difference between a usable ambient-noise dataset and noise.

HEALTHKIT timeInDaylight IS THE FREE ANSWER TO AMBIENT LIGHT, AND ALMOST NOBODY REACHES FOR IT. Everyone chasing ambient light on iOS goes to SensorKit (gated) or ARKit (foreground-only). Meanwhile the Apple Watch has been continuously sampling its ambient light sensor and writing a daylight-exposure aggregate into HealthKit since iOS 17 — retrievable with a plain HKStatisticsCollectionQuery, no entitlement, no approval, and with the ENTIRE retroactive history already sitting in the store on first launch. For circadian/light-exposure research this is 80% of the value of SensorKit's ambientLightSensor at 0% of the cost.

CoreMotion GIVES YOU ~7 DAYS OF DATA THE INSTANT YOU INSTALL. Both CMPedometer.queryPedometerData(from:to:) and CMMotionActivityManager.queryActivityStarting(from:to:) read a system-maintained cache that predates your app. A brand-new install can immediately reconstruct a week of step counts, floors climbed, and stationary/walking/running/automotive/cycling context with confidence levels. Most developers wire up live updates and never call the query variants, throwing away a free week of history on every install and reinstall.

CMMotionActivity FLAGS ARE NOT MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, AND ALL-FALSE IS A VALID STATE. Apple's example: a car stopped at a red light reports automotive AND stationary both true. And 'it's also possible for all of the properties to be set to false when the device is in motion but the movement doesn't correlate to walking, running, cycling, or automotive travel.' Code written as an if/else-if chain over these booleans will silently mislabel a large fraction of samples. Also: empty query ranges return a CMErrorUnknown error rather than an empty array.

CLVisit RELAUNCHES A TERMINATED APP — NO BACKGROUND MODE REQUIRED. Apple: 'If your app is terminated while this service is active, the system relaunches your app when new visit events are ready to be delivered.' You do not declare a UIBackgroundModes entry, you do not run a persistent process, and battery cost is negligible because it rides the same cell/Wi-Fi infrastructure as significant-location-change. For a sideloaded personal logger this is the single most robust unattended collection primitive on iOS — more reliable than BGTaskScheduler, which the system throttles aggressively. It also works WITHOUT precise-location authorization, degrading to reduced accuracy rather than failing.

THE MAGNETOMETER IS A FREE, UNPERMISSIONED ENVIRONMENT SENSOR. Raw CMMagnetometerData requires no usage-description key at all. Steel-framed buildings, elevators, motors, transformers, laptops, induction cooktops and vehicles all produce distinctive magnetic signatures, making it a viable indoor/outdoor classifier and even a coarse room-identity fingerprint. A second free signal falls out of CoreLocation for nothing: CLHeading.headingAccuracy degrading sharply is itself an indicator of local magnetic interference, i.e. 'I am indoors or in a vehicle'.

CMAltimeter IS THE FREE BAROMETER AND IT IS UNDERUSED AS AN ENVIRONMENT SENSOR. CMAltitudeData.pressure gives raw kPa at ~1 Hz for the cost of one Info.plist key. Beyond altitude, the pressure trace detects weather fronts (slow multi-hour drift), indoor/outdoor transitions and HVAC cycling (small step changes), door and window openings (transients), and elevator rides. Apple generates events at regular intervals 'regardless of whether the data has changed', so you get a clean uniformly-sampled series. Battery cost is very low. Note the hardware split Apple documents explicitly: relative altitude is broadly available, but ABSOLUTE altitude is iPhone 12+ and Apple Watch Series 6/SE+ only.

UIScreen.brightness IS AN INDIRECT AMBIENT LIGHT SENSOR READOUT WITH ZERO PERMISSION. When auto-brightness is on, iOS drives this value from the ambient light sensor. Reading it costs nothing, prompts nothing, and works while your app is foreground. It is confounded by manual adjustment and Low Power Mode, but as a cheap continuous companion signal to correlate against ARKit spot readings it is free information almost everyone ignores. Caveat from Apple: WRITING to it persists until device lock — read-only is safe.

OPEN-METEO'S ARCHIVE LETS YOU RETROACTIVELY ENRICH YOUR ENTIRE EXISTING HISTORY — WEATHERKIT CANNOT. archive-api.open-meteo.com serves hourly reanalysis data from 1940 to present for arbitrary coordinates, free and keyless. Combined with HealthKit's full retroactive store and CoreLocation history, you can join years of past biometrics against the actual weather, pressure, daylight duration and solar radiation at your location on each day. WeatherKit only offers climatological comparisons, not arbitrary historical observations. Open-Meteo also exposes PM2.5, PM10, ozone, NO2, SO2, CO, aerosol optical depth, dust and birch/grass/ragweed pollen via its air-quality endpoint — an entire environmental exposure axis Apple exposes nowhere on iOS.

SRAmbientLightSample CARRIES MORE THAN LUX — INCLUDING WHICH SENSOR SAW IT. It exposes .lux, a .chromaticity struct with CIE x and y coordinates, and .placement (SensorPlacement) identifying front vs back sensor. Chromaticity is what separates warm incandescent light from daylight from blue-heavy screen light — the actually interesting variable for circadian work, and strictly more informative than a scalar lux value. Apple's own docs list only 'ambient light information' in the abstract; you have to open the sample type to discover this.

iOS 26 AND 27 SHOW APPLE ACTIVELY EXPANDING SENSORKIT, NOT DEPRECATING IT. iOS 26 added SRSensor.acousticSettings and .sleepSessions. iOS 27 beta added .headphoneMotion (AirPods acceleration, rotation rate AND altitude, as [CMRecordedDeviceMotion]) and .headphoneSettings, plus an entirely new SRReader<Sensor: SRDataSensor> generic async/await API with 24 per-sensor types replacing the delegate-based SRSensorReader. The four newest sensors still ship with raw header-comment stubs as documentation — Apple's own text includes the typo 'Sesnor stream for sleep sessions collection' — which is a reliable tell that these landed recently and were not doc-reviewed.

SEPARATE THE THREE ENTITLEMENT TIERS WHEN PLANNING — THEY ARE NOT A SPECTRUM. Tier 1, Info.plist + runtime prompt only, works on a FREE Apple ID: SoundAnalysis, AVAudioSession metering, HealthKit (all environmental types), CoreMotion (altimeter, magnetometer, pedometer, motion activity, headphone motion), CoreLocation (visits, heading), ARKit, AVCaptureDevice, UIScreen, NWPathMonitor, Open-Meteo. Tier 2, self-enabled capability requiring a PAID account but NO Apple approval: WeatherKit, Wi-Fi info. Tier 3, Apple must approve you and an organization account is mandatory: SensorKit. The practical consequence is that a free-Apple-ID sideloaded app can reach essentially everything in Tier 1 — which covers ambient sound classification, calibrated ambient dB, daylight exposure, barometric pressure, magnetic field, visit detection, motion context and full weather enrichment. The gap versus SensorKit is real but narrower than it first appears: what you genuinely cannot replicate is lux with chromaticity, keyboard metrics, speech metrics, device/messages/phone usage reports, and raw PPG/ECG waveforms.
